messages:

Subject: Follow-up: Helio Platform inference needs & SLO targets

Diego —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the bits we promised to share:

Summary of what we discussed
- Primary use: real-time transcription + medical entity extraction for our telehealth assistant.
- Peak vs steady: expected steady-state ~120 QPS, typical bursts up to ~2,000 QPS for 60-120s during morning window.
- Tokens per request: average 700 tokens (prompt + expected output), 95th perc ~1,900 tokens.
- Latency target: 95th percentile end-to-end < 200ms for non-streamed inference; streaming partial transcripts acceptable as low as 50ms chunking.
- Concurrency: up to ~300 concurrent open sessions during peak.
- Streaming requirement: we need server-initiated partial responses (chunked transcripts) as audio is consumed.

Ask: can Redwood provide a quick throughput sizing estimate (tokens/sec and QPS) and confirm whether streaming chunk sizes map cleanly to your streaming latency SLOs? Also let us know any constraints around regional routing (we prefer US-West).

Attaching a small sample of our anonymized traffic and the recording from the demo for your ops team.

Attachments: heliodiag_sample_traffic.csv, call_recording_20260914.mp3

Next steps from our side:
- I can share a slightly larger sample export if that helps sizing.
- Procurement is ready to start the commercial conversation pending a sizing + cost estimate.

Best,

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Helio Platform inference needs & SLO targets

Andrew —

Appreciate the clear recap and the sample. Quick note from our side after a fast read-through: everything you described is feasible, but the exact sizing (tokens/sec and QPS) depends a lot on a couple of distribution details. A few clarifying questions and an initial plan below.

Clarifying Qs (would speed up a precise estimate)
- Peak window duration: you mentioned 60-120s bursts — is that continuous user activity (i.e., steady arrival rate) or a rapid fan-out where many sessions open within 10s and ramp down?
- Token mix: can you confirm how often the 95th perc ~1,900 tokens occurs vs the 700-token median? A rough percentiles CSV is ideal.
- Streaming chunk size: when you say 50ms chunking, do you expect server-to-client partial transcripts every 50ms of audio, or do you buffer to produce text every 200-500ms? This affects per-request small-token overhead.
- Concurrency definition: when you say 300 concurrent open sessions, is that actively generating tokens (i.e., GPU compute) or mostly idle session handles with occasional writes?

Initial sizing notes (very rough)
- If steady 120 QPS at ~700 tokens -> ~84k tokens/sec steady. For bursts at 2,000 QPS with median token size, you’re ~1.4M tokens/sec. If many requests hit 1.9k tokens, peak could rise to ~3.8M tokens/sec.
- For streaming with frequent small chunks, the per-chunk overhead increases latency-sensitive compute; we typically map streaming with 200–500ms chunk windows for medical audio to balance cost and latency.

Proposed next steps
1) Please upload a small percentile CSV (p50/p75/p90/p95/p99) per hour for a typical day — we can use that to create a conservative throughput plan. I’ve attached a short template that helps us map tokens->GPU throughput.
2) Marissa will run a quick ops sizing and propose Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for the pilot. Monica will pull sample cost delta estimates for steady vs burst provisioning.
3) Book a 45-min sizing deep dive early next week — propose Tue 16th or Wed 17th.

I attached our template: throughput_template.csv

Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Looping in a couple quick ops comments before the sizing call:
- For pilot, recommend Hosted API with burstable Dedicated policy (reservations + burst) so Helio can avoid overcommit while we characterize traffic.
- We should request a day of 1:1 traffic replay (anonymized) to validate prefix/cache hit assumptions and streaming behavior.
- I’ll prepare two config options: (A) latency-optimized (lower quantization, higher unit cost) and (B) cost-optimized (QAT/8-bit where acceptable).

I’ll draft the short sizing worksheet now and attach it to the calendar invite.

—Marissa
Director, Performance & Solutions
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Diego / team —

Thanks. Uploaded the percentile CSV and a slightly larger anonymized sample to the S3 link below. The attached small CSV (heliodiag_sample_traffic.csv) contains p50/p75/p90/p95/p99 per hour for a 72-hour window.

S3: https://s3.amazonaws.com/heliodiag-samples/hl00218_sample_traffic.csv
Attachments: heliodiag_sample_traffic.csv, call_recording_20260914.mp3

Answers to your Qs:
- Burst pattern: fan-out over ~8–12s when a clinic session opens (many participants open simultaneously), then steady arrivals follow for the remainder of the morning window.
- Token mix: 700 tokens median is ~65% of requests, 1.9k+ tokens are ~6% of requests (mostly long consults).
- Streaming chunking: we typically emit every 300ms of audio -> text chunks roughly every 250–400 tokens depending on language.
- Concurrency: ~300 are active compute sessions at peak (not idle handles).

We’re good to meet Tue 16 Sep at 10:00 PT — I’ll accept the invite once you send it. Procurement is on standby for the commercial discussion pending sizing.

Best,
Andrew
